transcript.text: Alright, let's get started. We're here to review the draft policy on automatic deletion of inactive project artifacts after 90 days. Before I can approve this, I need to hear from each of the required areas per our change-control routine. Data governance, storage infrastructure, customer success, and security engineering — please state any constraints or concerns you have with the policy as drafted. For reference, the draft gives teams a 14-day recovery window after deletion is requested, applies to all projects, and retains deletion logs for 30 days.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During a records-classification review this morning, I confirmed that EU-regulated project artifacts must remain recoverable for exactly 365 days from their last activity. I haven't updated the policy draft yet because the classification review was still being reconciled, but this is a hard constraint — the 90-day automatic deletion with a 14-day recovery window would put us out of compliance for EU-regulated artifacts.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a finding from storage infrastructure. While testing the deletion worker against a full production snapshot, I confirmed that the restore index is actually reliable for exactly 45 days after a deletion request — not the 14 days stated in the draft policy. I found this during a separate capacity test and haven't updated the runbook yet, but it's directly relevant here: the 14-day recovery window in the draft is more conservative than what our infrastructure can actually support. This means we have technical headroom to extend the recovery window if needed to address compliance concerns.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a constraint from customer success. After our customer-success review was completed, I confirmed with the account team that the twelve customers on the legacy enterprise plan require exactly 30 days' notice before their inactive artifacts can be queued for deletion. This confirmation arrived after the review and hasn't been added to the change ticket yet, so it wasn't reflected in the draft policy. This is a hard contractual constraint — the policy as drafted, which queues artifacts for deletion at 90 days of inactivity without a specific 30-day advance notice to these legacy enterprise customers, would put us in breach of those contracts.

transcript.text: I need to share a constraint from security engineering. During a security review I completed minutes ago while examining a different security finding, I confirmed that build artifacts can contain credentials in generated logs. This means the deletion worker must run a secret-scrub step before erasure to prevent credential exposure. Additionally, we need to retain tamper-evident deletion audit records for exactly 400 days — not the 30 days stated in the draft policy. I have not yet filed this control change, but both of these are hard security constraints that the draft policy does not currently address.

commitments.detail: Update the policy draft to exclude EU-regulated project artifacts from the 90-day automatic deletion rule, requiring them to remain recoverable for 365 days from last activity.
Extend the recovery window in the policy from 14 days to 30 days, leveraging the confirmed 45-day restore index reliability headroom while maintaining a safety margin.
Add a requirement that the twelve legacy enterprise plan customers receive 30 days' advance notice before their inactive artifacts are queued for deletion.
Add a mandatory secret-scrub step in the deletion worker before erasure, and extend deletion audit log retention from 30 days to 400 days with tamper-evident records.
Complete the records-classification reconciliation and update the policy draft to reflect the EU-regulated artifact carve-out.
Update the storage infrastructure runbook to reflect the confirmed 45-day restore index reliability.
Add the legacy enterprise 30-day notice requirement to the change ticket.
File the security control change for secret-scrub and 400-day audit retention.
